wretch: A miserable person; one profoundly unhappy.
wretched: Very miserable; sunk in, or accompanied by, deep affliction or distress, as from want, anxiety, or grief.
wretchedness: The quality or state of being wretched.
wring: To twist and compress; to turn and strain with violence.
wringing: a. & n. from Wring, v. Wringing machine, a wringer.
wrinkle: A winkle. A small ridge, prominence, or furrow formed by the shrinking or contraction of any smooth substance.
writ: 3d pers. sing. pres. of Write, for writeth.
write: To set down, as legible characters.
writer: One who writes, or has written; a scribe.
writing: The act or art of forming letters and characters on paper, wood, stone, or other material, for the purpose of recording the ideas which characters and words express, or of…
wrong: imp. of Wring. Wrung. Chaucer. Twisted.
wrote: To root with the snout. See 1st.
wrought: imp. & p. p. of Work. Alas that I was wrought !.
yarn: Spun wool; woolen thread; also, thread of other material, as of cotton, flax, hemp, or silk.
ye: You — the old second-person plural pronoun.
yea: Yes; ay; a word expressing assent, or an affirmative, or an affirmative answer to a question, now superseded by yes.
year: The time of the apparent revolution of the sun trough the ecliptic.
yearly: Happening, accruing, or coming every year.
yearn: To pain; to grieve; to vex. "She laments, sir, for it, that it would yearn your heart to see it.".
yell: To cry out, or shriek, with a hideous noise.
yellow: Being of a bright saffronlike color.
yes: Ay; yea; -- a word which expresses affirmation or consent.
yesterday: The day last past; the day next before the present.
yesternight: The last night; the night last past.
yet: Any one of several species of large marine gastropods belonging to the genus Yetus, or Cymba.
yield: To give in return for labor expended.
yielding: Inclined to give way, or comply; flexible.
yoke: A bar or frame of wood by which two oxen are joined at the heads or necks for working together.
yokefellow: An associate or companion in, or as in.
yonder: At a distance, but within view. Yonder are two apple women scolding.
you: The pronoun of the second person, in the nominative, dative, and objective case, indicating the person or persons addressed.
young: Not long born; still in the first part of life.
your: The form of the possessive case of the personal pronoun you.
yours: See the Note under Your. See the Note under.
youth: The quality or state of being young.
youthful: Not yet mature or aged; young. "Two youthful knights.".
zeal: Passionate ardor in the pursuit of anything.
zealous: Filled with, or characterized by, zeal.
zif: The second month of the Jewish ecclesiastical year, corresponding to our.
zillah: A district or local division, as of a province.
zion: (Jewish Antiq.) A hill in Jerusalem, which, after the capture of that city by the Israelites, became the royal residence of David and his successors.
zohar: A Jewish cabalistic book attributed by tradition to Rabbi Simon ben Yochi, who lived about the end of the 1st century, a.
